question: Who won the Sahitya Akademi Award 2025 for writing on the exploration of tribal voices in rural Indian society in Jharkhand?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Parvati Tirkey**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Parvati Tirkey**, an emerging **Oraon tribal poet** from **Jharkhand**, has been honored with the **Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar 2025** for her contribution to **Hindi literature**.
 
• She received the award for her acclaimed poetry collection titled **"Phir Ugan"**, which focuses on the exploration of **tribal voices** and the cultural essence of **rural Jharkhand**.
 
• Her work is significant for documenting the **struggles, aspirations, and socio-cultural identity** of the **indigenous communities**, particularly the **Oraon tribe**, in the face of modernization.
 
• The poetry in **"Phir Ugan"** brings to light the **marginalized narratives** of **rural India**, bridging the gap between **tribal oral traditions** and mainstream **written literature**.
 
• By winning this award, **Parvati Tirkey** has established herself as a vital voice in **contemporary Indian literature**, representing the **Chota Nagpur** region's unique heritage. ***Hence, the correct answer is Parvati Tirkey.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar**:

 
 
• It is a **literary honor** in India established in **2011** by the **Sahitya Akademi**, India's **National Academy of Letters**.
 
• The award is specifically designed to recognize and promote **young writers** under the **age of 35** who write in any of the **24 recognized Indian languages**.
 
• The prize includes a **casket** containing an engraved **copper plaque** and a **cheque of Rs. 50,000**.
 
 
 
• **Geetanjali Shree**:
 
 
• She is a renowned **Hindi novelist** and short-story writer based in **New Delhi**.
 
• She made history by winning the **International Booker Prize** in **2022** for her novel **"Ret Samadhi"** (translated as **Tomb of Sand**).
 
• Her work often explores **familial relationships**, **partition**, and **women's identity** in **North India**.
 
 
 
• **Ruskin Bond**:
 
 
• A prolific **Indian author** of **British descent**, living in **Landour, Mussoorie**.
 
• He was awarded the **Sahitya Akademi Award** in **1992** for **"Our Trees Still Grow in Dehra"**.
 
• He is a recipient of the **Padma Shri (1999)** and **Padma Bhushan (2014)** for his immense contribution to **children's literature** and **Indian writing in English**.
 
 
 
• **Perumal Murugan**:
 
 
• He is a highly influential **Tamil writer** and scholar known for his novels, short stories, and poems.
 
• His famous works include **"Madhorubhagan"** (One Part Woman) and **"Poonachi"**.
 
• He has won several awards, including the **Sahitya Akademi Award** for **Translation** and was shortlisted for the **International Booker Prize** in **2023** for his novel **"Pyre"**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sahitya Akademi**: Founded on **12 March 1954**, it is an autonomous organization under the **Ministry of Culture**, Government of India.
 
• **Languages Covered**: The Akademi recognizes **24 languages**, which include the **22 languages** listed in the **Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India**, along with **English** and **Rajasthani**.
 
• **Significance of Jharkhand Literature**: The region is known for its rich **Adivasi literature**, which focuses on **"Jal, Jangal, Jameen"** (Water, Forest, Land) and the **social justice** movements of the **Munda, Santhal, and Oraon** tribes.
